{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjdzc8AAAABa6SoMw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IVzhEf5_0", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IV", "number": 83, "title": "Implement BIOS-visible Saturn startup hardware initialization and MMIO sequencing", "body": "## Problem

The emulator has substantial SH-2, SMPC, SCU, CD, VDP and SCSP support, and its **BIOS-less HLE disc** path executes the original Star Collector, Prism Courier and Hardware Lab guests. However, that successful HLE path bypasses critical BIOS-visible startup behavior. At checked `main` `8f1cdc14031009a190d9760f6ea3346ceafc8831`, the documented **ExternalBios** mode uses real reset vectors but commonly faults on missing device/register or bus behavior, and does not establish a complete firmware-to-disc handoff. Thus we cannot yet demonstrate that a firmware program can initialize the console using ordinary hardware accesses and boot an executable from media.

The next critical step toward **eventual commercial-game compatibility** is an independently validated **external-firmware startup hardware sequence**: reset → initialization of the required hardware subsystems through authentic MMIO and interrupts → CD startup/transfer → first-read program handoff, without silently switching to HLE or relying on host-manufactured guest state.

**Do not claim commercial-game support, stock Sega BIOS compatibility or completed Saturn hardware conformance as an outcome of this task.** This is a deliberately bounded, hardware-focused integration milestone.

## Expected outcome

Implement the **smallest evidence-backed set of missing hardware register behavior, startup ordering, reset boundaries, interrupts and bus/CD transactions** needed for a self-authored, executable **512 KiB synthetic BIOS ROM** to cold-boot through the genuine **ExternalBios** path and load/transfer control to an original synthetic disc program **via the emulated hardware interfaces**.

The synthetic firmware must exercise real SH-2 instructions and real scheduled device/SCU/CD transactions, not host-side HLE installation or host-written pass records. It should perform a representative, primary-manual-derived startup sequence such as:
- Reset vector acquisition, stack/vector establishment, BSC/cache/CPU-local prerequisites as needed.
- SMPC and system-controller sequencing for the relevant SH-2, slave/sound/CD reset or enable state and command completion/interrupts.
- SCU mask/vector setup, accepted IRQs and DMA/transaction fences.
- CD initialization, status/TOC, selection and retrieval of synthetic first-read executable sectors, and correct transfer completion.
- The required video or other observable device initialization, then **actual guest control transfer** to the loaded program.

The original disc guest must independently verify initialized device state, executable/data bytes, correct entry PC/stack, IRQ and DMA effects, restart, and observable native/production Wasm results. Add only behavior justified by primary documentation or an explicitly labeled deterministic convention where electrical timing is unspecified. Reuse the existing CD/SMPC/SCU/BIOS and test infrastructure instead of building a second emulator or BIOS service layer.

## Context and reproduction

Repository: [takahirox/saturn-rust](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust).

Existing source/contracts to inspect **before** implementing:
- [`docs/architecture.md`](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/docs/architecture.md): ExternalBios is separate from BIOS-less HLE and external Sega BIOS execution remains incomplete; media loading, CD and device components are partial.
- [`docs/hardware-conformance.md`](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/docs/hardware-conformance.md): outstanding BIOS reset/MMIO/service startup and CD command/timing/error/bus requirements. Note that some prose still says Issue #17 is open; GitHub actually closed #17 as a **partial checkpoint**, and incomplete hardware requirements are still outstanding.
- [`src/hle/README.md`](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/src/hle/README.md): original guest-executed HLE services are **installed only for HLE mode**. Preserve this isolation. Existing independently generated synthetic ROM/clock guests and reset tests are useful foundations.
- `src/lib.rs`, `src/cpu.rs`, `src/bus.rs`, `src/onchip.rs`, `src/smpc.rs`, `src/scu.rs`, `src/cd.rs`, `src/disc.rs`, `src/media.rs` and relevant `tests/boot.rs`, `tests/sh2_system.rs`, `tests/clock.rs`, `tests/cd*.rs`, `tests/hle_system.rs`, `scripts/browser-smoke.mjs`.
- Recent [PR #82](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/pull/82), [#78](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/pull/78), [#76](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/pull/76) and [#70](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/pull/70) already added CPU interrupt, standby, CD and instruction pipeline behavior. Preserve and integrate them; avoid reopening solved increments.

Use **primary Saturn manuals**, reconciled by revision and scope. Relevant starting references include the [Saturn Boot ROM User's Manual](https://github.com/luckyseoul/saturn-docs/blob/main/files/ST-079B-R3-011895.pdf), [System Program ST-162-R1](https://github.com/luckyseoul/saturn-docs/blob/main/files/ST-162-R1-092994.pdf), [Saturn Disc Format Standards ST-040](https://github.com/luckyseoul/saturn-docs/blob/main/files/ST-040-R4-051795.pdf), [SH7604 Hardware Manual](https://antime.kapsi.fi/sega/files/sh7604.pdf), applicable [SMPC](https://antime.kapsi.fi/sega/files/ST-169-R3-061694.pdf) and SCU/CD references already indexed in the conformance matrix. Validate actual page/section references before relying on them; do not invent register behavior to accommodate a fixture.

**Reproduction before implementation:** construct the minimal original external-ROM + original synthetic media test harness, record reset/initialization/MMIO/SCU/CD/IRQ trace, and demonstrate one or more *specific* missing or incorrect production hardware behaviors against the inherited `main` without suppressing errors. Identify which observable barrier is being removed and why it is a hardware defect rather than a BIOS fixture assumption.

This Issue is a **bounded synthetic boot-path milestone**; full proprietary Sega BIOS services, security/area executables, authenticated retail media and general game support remain separate future work.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Primary-grounded startup contract:** document an executable stage/deadline and MMIO sequence for the external-firmware boot path, mapping each firmware operation to existing or missing registers, reset/clock ownership, bus grants, interrupt acknowledgment, and relevant primary manuals. Clearly distinguish hardware-required behavior, explicit emulator conventions and still-unsupported BIOS functionality. Do not duplicate or replace existing HLE behavior.
- [ ] **Real external BIOS entry:** generate an original MIT-licensed 512 KiB synthetic firmware image with genuine reset vectors and SH-2 instructions. Boot it in `ExternalBios` (not HLE). Preserve the selected ROM, medium and reset state through the supported local/native and Wasm boot APIs; if selecting both firmware and media is not currently possible, implement the minimal necessary explicit selection flow without fallback, uploads or persistence of private bytes.
- [ ] **Implement missing device functionality:** implement—not merely stub, swallow or whitelist—the **specific missing hardware MMIO, bus ordering, SMPC/SCU/CD startup, clock/reset, interrupt and transfer behavior** revealed by the baseline and needed by the defined startup trace. Reads/writes must cause their documented observable consequences and proper waits/faults. Avoid test-address magic, ROM-signature detection, synthetic-firmware-specific fast paths or arbitrary returns on unimplemented ports.
- [ ] **Real media loading/handoff:** use a synthetic Saturn IP/ISO9660 or suitable original raw-media fixture through the current media/CD model. Firmware must issue documented CD commands and/or DMA/CPU FIFO reads to copy **actual disc bytes** into executable RAM, verify transfer completion, set up context and **jump to those bytes**. The host may mount authorized local media but must not copy the first-read program to RAM, jump to its entry point or prewrite result records on behalf of ExternalBios. HLE mode's existing host/guest bootstrap remains distinct.
- [ ] **Independent executable oracles:** author literal expected records for ordered MMIO transactions, accepted/pending IRQs, DMA transfers, CD status/data and reset effects, stack/PC/entry, loaded instruction bytes and the executing disc guest's computed results. At least one unchanged negative control must fail on inherited `main` and pass after the production implementation. Mutate input sectors/operands, omit a required command, and exercise invalid/no-media paths: they must fail or report an explicit documented status rather than coincidentally reach the success marker.
- [ ] **Time and state integrity:** test before/at/after critical command and bus deadlines, rejected or pending transactions, canceled/restarted commands, reset and SYSRES/cold boot boundaries, retained backup versus cleared volatile state, master/slave isolation and SCU IRQ/DMA effects. Compare chunk advancement (e.g. 1/3/17/10000) and passive/debug inspection to ensure the guest trace and results do not depend on observation frequency. Never replace clocked hardware with instantaneous host services.
- [ ] **Production browser coverage:** register fixture build/check commands and a real browser smoke group running the same original firmware and disc bytes under production Rust→Wasm, `/saturn-rust/` path, with observable guest state/Canvas/controls as appropriate. Exercise both external-firmware and existing HLE modes to prove mode isolation, local media privacy (no uploaded BIOS/disc bytes), no fallback, and valid restart behavior.
- [ ] **Preserve existing quality:** all existing Star Collector, Prism Courier and Hardware Lab runs, current 1,122+ Rust tests, 69+ browser groups, 99+ fixture checks, native/Wasm hardware/interrupt/DMA/CPU/media oracles, CI failure propagation and Pages publication gating must remain complete and passing. Do not drop tests or weaken expected pixel/PCM/clock/error assertions to make the new boot path pass.
- [ ] **Verify autonomously before merge:** run `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo build --locked`, `cargo test --locked`, native/Wasm `cargo clippy --locked ... -- -D warnings`, `sh scripts/check-fixtures.sh`, `sh scripts/build-web.sh`, `node --test scripts/ci-runner.test.mjs`, and complete `npm run test:browser`. Require all applicable PR GitHub Actions jobs to pass; include independent traces, failed inherited-main controls, fixture hashes and exact counts in `docs/validation-issue-83.md` (or corresponding actual Issue number). Update architecture/conformance notes for *proved* behavior and remaining omissions.
- [ ] **Honest scope and handoff:** document which firmware boot/hardware stages are verified and which remain unsupported (especially stock Sega BIOS menu/boot, region/security sequence, full BIOS libraries, CD drive corner cases and commercial titles). Completing this synthetic scenario is **not** a claim that any commercial game or original Sega BIOS boots. Any follow-up prerequisites should be recorded as actionable gaps, not hidden behind a success flag.

## Optional validation

Additional independently authored startup variants, programmed BSC wait states, raw mixed-mode media, different PLL/area profiles, and extra negative controls are welcome if they can be executed autonomously. Licensed/open-source homebrew can help independently corroborate behavior, but proprietary BIOS/discs, a physical console, human manual tests and subjective visual/audio signoff are **not required**.

## Required post-merge verification

None. Fully validate all required behavior on the implementation/PR before merge. The existing main-only CI Pages deployment remains gated on all required checks; do not require live-site inspection or human approval to complete this Issue.

## Related work

Related to #17 (historical partial umbrella hardware checkpoint), #69/#70 (IF/ID), #75/#76 (CD R–W), #77/#78 (standby) and #81/#82 (interrupt acquisition). Keep partial hardware conformance and actual retail compatibility explicitly distinct from this scoped synthetic BIOS boot milestone.
